feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Iteration 9 (271.06, ±0.03 m, y=0.04, 0.016 footprint, kd 0.35) is the best raced platform. Its slalom line_loss_events is still 1.0 and slalom progress about 0.10, so the wheel_track lever is the one still untested. Iteration 8 repeated iteration 7 exactly, so single-variable tests here are reliable. The controller is held fixed so the race isolates wheel_track. Read the next race as follows. If the score holds at or near 271 with oval completions kept, keep wheel_track 0.14 and move to a single further step only if slalom line loss is still at or above 1. If oval completions fall and the score drops well below 271, the steering gain has dropped; return to 0.12 or test 0.10, and do not change body or mass. Iterations 2 and 3 showed that body changes cost progress, so body_length, mass and body_width should stay fixed.
requested_changes: If the score is at or near 271 with oval completions held and slalom line_loss_events below 1: keep wheel_track at 0.14 and keep sensor_positions at x = ±0.03, y = 0.04, sensor_size 0.016. Evidence: iteration 9 (271.06) with the same layout and controller, and iteration 8 reproducing iteration 7 exactly.

If oval completions fall below 8 of 20 and the score drops well below 271: return wheel_track to 0.12, or test 0.10 as a single change. Evidence: the iteration 9 oval finished 8 of 20 with mean progress 0.91; a lower steering gain from a wider track is the likely cause if completions fall.
Do not change body_length, body_width or mass. Evidence: iteration 2 (0.14 m, 0.6 kg) cut s-bend progress from 0.16 to 0.1275, and iteration 3 recovered it on the baseline body.
